leaks.name: The click instrument counts crawlers; it grew 473% in three days

store_setup_share.note: the 7 setup-index srcs; something walked the 89 setup pages and followed every Buy Pro link

evidence.root_cause: billing/src/index.js scripted-UA test was `/^(curl|python|node|wget|go-http|undici|axios|httpie)/i` OR `!looksLikeNavigation`, and looksLikeNavigation was satisfied by `accept: text/html`, which every crawler sends. Start-anchored, so `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1)` and `... HeadlessChrome/120` both walked past it.
evidence.live_control: GET /buy/a3-nonexistent-product?src=probe.a3.googlebot with the Googlebot UA and accept: text/html, no probe header. The dead-route branch records a click and never touches Stripe, so this measures the guard with no Stripe object created. Result recorded in live_control_result below.

live_control_result.conclusion: the live worker counted a Googlebot UA with accept: text/html as a human click; no x-mcp-probe header was sent and the 404 branch creates no Stripe object

leaks.size: 1685 recorded clicks, of which the number that can be shown to be a person is 3 (0.18%). The instrument has never produced a usable number.
leaks.fix: Counting is now opt-IN on the Fetch Metadata pair (sec-fetch-mode: navigate AND sec-fetch-dest: document), the UA denylists are unanchored, an untagged hit is bucketed as unattributed.<id> and excluded from the headline totals, and counters are written under a fresh `click:v2:` prefix so the contaminated v1 numbers are reported separately under `legacy` instead of being summed in.
leaks.test: billing/test/funnel-r1.test.mjs :: CONTROL: one identifiable human click moves the counter by exactly one, and nothing else does

connect_page_minting.defect: GET and HEAD /mcp/connect minted an anonymous token on EVERY request
connect_page_minting.cost_per_request: 1 KV read + 2 KV writes; the tok: key holds a data space for ANON_TTL = 30 days
connect_page_minting.rate_limit: TOKEN_MINTS_PER_IP = 10 per IP per hour; the 11th returns HTTP 429
connect_page_minting.why_it_mattered_now: this page became the hero destination of all 30 product pages and every /llms.txt line in this pass, and was about to enter the sitemap
connect_page_minting.worst_case: a NAT, VPN exit or office proxy generating 11 loads in an hour takes the entry point to the whole free tier off the air for everyone behind that address

live_proof.method: two consecutive GET /mcp/connect with a Googlebot UA and no browser headers, against the live worker

connect_page_minting.fix: mint only for a real browser navigation (sec-fetch-mode: navigate + sec-fetch-dest: document, unanchored bot/tool UA denylist) or an explicit ?mint=1; prefetches excluded via sec-purpose; HEAD never mints and returns no body. Everything else gets the same complete page with <token> placeholders and one 'Get my free token' link.
connect_page_minting.verdict: adding /mcp/connect to the sitemap WITHOUT this fix would have been the wrong trade
